sources.note: Sunbury, Cranbourne and Pakenham lines now run through the new tunnel spine (Arden, Parkville, State Library, Town Hall, Anzac), not the City Loop and not Flinders Street. Town Hall <-> Flinders Street interchange via the Degraves Street Subway; State Library <-> Melbourne Central interchange via the underground concourse. GTFS CONFIRMS a further structural fact the first pass did not have: the Sunbury route_id's own trips only run Sunbury <-> Town Hall/State Library (the west tunnel half); the Cranbourne and Pakenham route_ids' own trips only run Town Hall/Anzac <-> Cranbourne/Pakenham (the east tunnel half, sharing the whole Anzac-Malvern-Caulfield-Dandenong trunk). A single physical Sunbury-to-Cranbourne working is two chained trip_ids under two different route_ids, joined at Town Hall — not one route_id spanning the whole corridor. See metroTunnel block and gtfs-reconciliation.md.

notes: City id melbourne is a SEPARATE city. Do not invent city=mel, city=ptv, city=vic, or city=us. Do not merge V/Line long-distance or Yarra Trams into this city id. Agency Metro Trains Melbourne (PTV/Transport Victoria). Modes v1: Metro Trains suburban rail only (PTV route_type = 0 equivalent / GTFS folder 2 Metropolitan Train). No Yarra Trams, no buses (incl. Night Bus), no SkyBus, no V/Line long-distance beyond the walk-up services carried in docs/melbourne-d1/open-data-feed-and-eligibility.md, no coaches, no interstate, no Melbourne Airport Rail / Suburban Rail Loop (not yet printed as open on the official train map).

SECOND PASS (20 Sep 2026): every line's stations[] below was reconciled against the official Victorian GTFS Schedule static feed (folder 2, Metropolitan Train; downloaded, not committed — see sources[] above). Full per-line before/after diff, with the feed's publication date, is in docs/melbourne-d1/gtfs-reconciliation.md. The first pass's hand-transcription (no browser/PDF/GTFS access) was materially wrong in multiple places: missing stations (Kensington on Craigieburn, Moreland on Upfield, Hawthorn/Glenferrie on the Burnley-group branches, Hawksburn/Toorak/Armadale/Parkdale/Mordialloc on Frankston, Laverton/Aircraft on Werribee, Williamstown Beach on Williamstown, West Richmond/North Richmond on Hurstbridge/Mernda, Bell on Mernda, Union and Tecoma/Ringwood East on Belgrave/Lilydale, Cardinia Road/East Pakenham on Pakenham, and the entire Anzac-Malvern-Caulfield-Dandenong trunk on Cranbourne/Pakenham), wrong order (the Belgrave/Lilydale Camberwell-Box Hill segment had East Camberwell out of sequence), a misspelling (Glenhuntly -> Glen Huntly), and a wrong doNotGroup attribution (Union is on Belgrave/Lilydale, not Pakenham/Cranbourne — see hazard-pack.md's H1 resolution). Do not re-transcribe from memory again; re-run the GTFS diff if the feed changes materially.
Timezone Australia/Melbourne HAS DST (AEDT/AEST). Do not copy Perth/Brisbane/Adelaide no-DST assumptions.

Hub lock: Flinders Street. It is the inner lock for the City Loop / cross-city surface groups (Sandringham direct; Frankston, Glen Waverley, Alamein, Belgrave, Lilydale, Hurstbridge, Mernda, Craigieburn, Upfield, Werribee, Williamstown, Racecourse via the loop or direct). Flinders Street is NOT on the Sunbury/Cranbourne/Pakenham Metro Tunnel spine — those three lines skip Flinders Street, North Melbourne, and the City Loop entirely after 1 Feb 2026 (see metroTunnel below). Existing dogfood catalog/probe conventions that use Flinders Street as the example stop are respected; do not contradict that lock for the non-tunnel line groups.

City Loop stations (Flagstaff, Melbourne Central, Parliament) plus the two surface hub buildings (Flinders Street, Southern Cross) are the shared inner set for the loop-serving line groups. Melbourne Central is City Loop only (not the tunnel). Parliament serves the Frankston/Sandringham-direction loop portal plus the Burnley-group loop portal, not every group. Town Hall is Metro Tunnel only (not the City Loop) and is a DIFFERENT building from Flinders Street, linked only by the surface Degraves Street Subway. State Library is Metro Tunnel only and is a DIFFERENT building from Melbourne Central, linked only by an underground concourse. GTFS confirms two distinct loop-traversal directions used by different line groups: the Burnley/Frankston-direction groups run Flinders St -> Southern Cross -> Flagstaff -> Melbourne Central -> Parliament -> (outbound), while the Northern-group lines (Craigieburn/Upfield, and pre-tunnel-era Sunbury) run the loop the OTHER way, Flinders St -> Parliament -> Melbourne Central -> Flagstaff -> North Melbourne -> (outbound), never touching Southern Cross on that via-loop working. See direction-model-memo.md for which lines use the loop vs run direct by time of day -- this file records the station graph, not the schedule pattern.

Southern Cross is shared by Metro Trains (all loop/direct groups except Sandringham/Frankston-when-direct) AND V/Line long-distance. Same physical building, doNotGroup by mode in hazard-pack (Southern Cross Metro vs Southern Cross V/Line) so a V/Line-only walk-up service is never silently dropped nor double counted against the Metro board.
Stony Point IS IN as a Metro line (Frankston-Stony Point diesel shuttle), confirmed by the official PTV route page and the Metro Trains line picker -- not V/Line.

Racecourse line (Showgrounds) is IN as a printed Metro special-events station, not a daily all-day spine. Runs for race days / shows only. 'Flemington Racecourse' as a SEPARATE stop could not be confirmed in this GTFS snapshot (2026-09-18 week; no race meeting that week) — see the open item in hazard-pack.md and gtfs-reconciliation.md. Do not re-insert it into stations[] without a snapshot that actually calls at it.

17 named line groups on the current Metro Trains picker: Alamein, Belgrave, Craigieburn, Cranbourne, Frankston, Glen Waverley, Hurstbridge, Lilydale, Mernda, Pakenham, Racecourse, Sandringham, Stony Point, Sunbury, Upfield, Werribee, Williamstown. 16 run as regular all-day service; Racecourse is special-events only. GTFS's routes.txt has an 18th route_id, 'City Circle' (aus:vic:vic-02-CCL:), a short Flinders Street-loop-Flinders Street shuttle NOT on the 17-line picker — kept OUT of this pack's lines[] as a hazard note only (see H3 in hazard-pack.md), matching the 'published map wins for line inventory' precedence rule.

Metro Tunnel through-running (passenger from 1 Feb 2026): Sunbury + Cranbourne + Pakenham now form one continuous corridor through Arden, Parkville, State Library, Town Hall, Anzac, bypassing Flinders Street / North Melbourne / the City Loop. GTFS models this as THREE separate route_ids each covering only half the corridor (Sunbury: Sunbury<->Town Hall/State Library; Cranbourne and Pakenham: Town Hall/Anzac<->their own terminus, sharing the whole Anzac-Malvern-Caulfield-Dandenong trunk), joined operationally at Town Hall via chained trip_ids, not one route_id end to end. See metroTunnel block below.

Board-eligibility verdicts for V/Line services calling at shared Metro stations (Southern Cross, Flinders Street, Richmond, Caulfield, Clayton, Dandenong, Pakenham, North Melbourne, Footscray, Sunshine, Broadmeadows) live in docs/melbourne-d1/open-data-feed-and-eligibility.md and are carried into hazard-pack.md, with the Maryborough/Shepparton/Bairnsdale/Swan Hill rows resolved in the second pass per docs/melbourne-d1/vline-reservation-check.md — see hazard-pack.md's Board eligibility section. No `undecided` rows remain.

This JSON does not carry stopIds -- Jim resolves GTFS stop_id / parent_station values against the static feed in folder 2 (Metropolitan Train) of the nested statewide zip, matched by name/alias, never by inventing IDs here. Parent-station structure confirmed in this pass: platform-level stops (location_type blank) carry parent_station pointing at a location_type=1 station row (e.g. stop_id '10117' 'Jordanville Station' -> parent_station 'vic:rail:JOR' -> location_type=1 'Jordanville Railway Station'); location_type=2 rows are entrances, location_type=3 rows are generic access nodes (bike racks etc.) — both also carry parent_station back to the same location_type=1 row. See jim-handoff.md.

cityLoop.note: Every loop-serving group runs via the loop for part of the timetable and direct (skipping Flagstaff/Melbourne Central/Parliament, calling only Flinders Street/Southern Cross) for the rest, reversing by time of day and by which portal that group is rostered to. GTFS confirms two distinct loop-traversal directions (Burnley/Frankston-direction groups via Southern Cross first; Northern-group lines the other way via Parliament first, never touching Southern Cross on that working) — both converge on the same three loop stations, just approached from opposite ends. See direction-model-memo.md -- this is the hardest hazard in the pack and needed Tim's copy decision on whether 'via City Loop' surfaces in the UI (decided 20 Sep 2026, folded into direction-model-memo.md).

metroTunnel.note: Sunbury (west) through-runs with Cranbourne and Pakenham (south-east) via the new twin tunnels. These three lines do NOT call Flinders Street, North Melbourne, or the City Loop. Town Hall interchanges to Flinders Street via the surface Degraves Street Subway; State Library interchanges to Melbourne Central via an underground concourse. CORRECTED in this pass: GTFS shows the physical join between the Sunbury route_id and the Cranbourne/Pakenham route_ids is at TOWN HALL, not 'Footscray on the west side and South Yarra on the east side' as the first pass guessed — Sunbury's own trips run Sunbury<->Town Hall/State Library (never reaching Anzac), and Cranbourne/Pakenham's own trips run Town Hall/Anzac<->their terminus (never reaching Arden/Parkville/State Library). A single Sunbury-to-Cranbourne working is two chained trip_ids under two different route_ids joined at Town Hall. No single hub-lock stop string exists on this spine -- see direction-model-memo.md.

V/Line long-distance beyond the walk-up services carried `in` per docs/melbourne-d1/open-data-feed-and-eligibility.md and docs/melbourne-d1/vline-reservation-check.md (Albury and Warrnambool are `out-reservation`, fully reserved; Shepparton, Bairnsdale and Swan Hill are `in` per the board-eligibility rule's §6 unreserved-carriage clause; Maryborough, Ararat and Echuca are `in`, verified unreserved).
